title: Bleibtreustrasse
html_source:
Bleibtreustrasse is in fact named after Georg Bleibtreu (1828-1892) a painter. However, his son, Karl Bleibtreu (1859-1928), a Shakespearian writer & critic is referred to in the later Scylla & Charybdis episode. There has been much research on the newspaper ad purported to have been read by Bloom on 16 June 1904. However, it appears that, though No 34 was occupied by a Jewish charity, this was not until 1908. Ironically, the younger Bleibtreu was a notorious & self-proclaimed anti-semite.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: The literal translation of Bleibtreustrasse is “Be Faithful Street,” which is ironic given Bloom’s thoughts.
